the magnetic behaviour of Pt13 in the NaY zeolites is determined by the variety of stable isomers that can be encapsulated in the zeolites, and that this variety is determined by geometrical constraints and by the van der Waals interactions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structural stability of Pt13 clusters encapsulated in the NaY zeolites is determined by the solid angle of the cluster vertex bound to the zeolite super-cage.
the magnetic behaviour of the clusters is strongly affected by the geometrical constraints of the zeolite.

, in the case of Pt nanoparticles in zeolite, the magnetic behaviour is dominated by the geometrical constraints of the zeolite, which can lead to a large variety of isomers, with different magnetic properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the magnetic properties of Pt13 clusters are strongly affected by the zeolite environment.
the presence of the zeolite stabilises the formation of clusters which are otherwise unstable.

the stability and magnetism of the encapsulated clusters are strongly affected by their interaction with the zeolite host, which is a key factor to take into account in the design of magnetic nanoparticles.
